title: Typhoon Champi Leaves One Dead and 500 Injured as It Exits Taiwan
summary:
Taiwan's northeastern coast was lashed by gusts of 191 km/h and waves as high as 26 feet on Friday as Typhoon Champi brought severe disruption to the island's infrastructure. The storm left one person dead and 500 injured, while knocking out power to more than 77,000 households and forcing the cancellation of nearly 1,000 flights. Local authorities shut down schools, offices, and financial markets, and work was suspended at TSMC's semiconductor fabrication plants in Hsinchu, though no fab damage or production disruptions were reported.

Champi tied a record for the strongest storm of 2026 with peak sustained winds of 185 mph. Prior to hitting Taiwan, the system passed within 10 miles of Guam as a Category 4 hurricane, reducing the territory's internet connectivity to 41% of normal levels. The storm is now tracking toward eastern China and Japan, with operators in Shanghai anticipating shipment delays.

🇬🇺 Earth’s strongest storm of 2026 now has a twin.

Super Typhoon Champi has exploded to Category 5-equivalent strength with 185 mph sustained winds, tying Super Typhoon Sinlaku for the top spot this year.

Just 3 days ago, it brushed past Guam as a Category 4, its center passing just 10 miles from the island. 

Even so, nearly half the island lost power. And it still wasn't done getting stronger.

Thankfully, Champi is now unleashing its fury over open water. Let’s hope it stays that way.

selectedTweets.text:
According to Korean media, Typhoon Champi has shut down most of TAIWAN today.

Schools, offices and financial markets are closed, and every one of the 262 domestic flights plus more than 350 international flights have been canceled.

Work in Hsinchu, home to $TSM's most important fabs, has also been suspended, and TSMC canceled its company sports day planned for tomorrow.

The storm is packing gusts of around 191 km/h and up to 900 mm of rain, but it is expected to skim the northeast coast rather than make a direct landfall.

So far there are no reports of any fab damage or production disruption.

Taiwan makes almost every advanced AI chip in the world, so this is one weather map every AI investor should be watching today.

JPMorgan expects $TSM to keep growing its CoWoS packaging capacity.

- 130,000 wafers a month by the end of 2026.

- 260,000 by the end of 2027.

- 320,000 by the end of 2028.

$INTC says its EMIB packaging is 30% to 40% cheaper.

But JPMorgan expects Intel's outside capacity to be only 7% to 10% of CoWoS by 2028, with yields around 60% on large AI chips versus 98% for TSMC.
